claim: The EPP's Data Layer operates asynchronously and watches the Kubernetes API server specifically for InferencePool and Pod object updates, which is the primary place where a Kubernetes-pod assumption is baked into the EPP.
stance_target: identifying where Kubernetes/pod assumptions live inside the EPP
scope_conditions: llm-d dev (unreleased) documentation as of Sep 2026, version dev branch
quoted_support: Asynchronously, the Data layer watches the Kubernetes API server for updates to relevant objects like InferencePools and Pods for endpoint discovery.

claim: The EPP is structured as four extensible components -- Request Handler (Parser plugins), Flow Control, Request Scheduler (Filter->Score->Pick), and Data Layer -- with the Ext-Proc Server itself explicitly marked non-extensible ('Extension is ill-advised').
stance_target: EPP internal component boundaries and which parts are meant to be customized
quoted_support: The Ext-Proc Server protocol is very well defined & specific, deviations could cause the EPP to become unusable or unstable. Extension is ill-advised.

claim: Custom request parsers are an explicitly supported extension point: users can write a parser for a non-default protocol, and the rest of EPP functionality is agnostic to the original request protocol.
stance_target: extensibility of EPP outside default OpenAI/vLLM-gRPC formats
quoted_support: In addition, users can write a custom parser for their own protocol. The rest of the functionality in EPP is agnostic to the original request protocol, enabling easy adaptation of the EPP to new request formats.

claim: The Data Layer's inputs already include non-Kubernetes sources by design: 'consultant' sidecars such as a latency predictor, kv-indexer, or tokenizer feed advanced routing decisions alongside Kube API and model-server metrics data.
stance_target: existence of a precedent extension path for non-pod / non-k8s data sources in the EPP
quoted_support: "Consultant" sidecars like the latency predictor, the kv-indexer or tokenizer for advanced routing

claim: The EPP configuration (EndpointPickerConfig YAML via --config-file or --config-text) is read only at process startup; no hot reload exists, so backend-type additions that only change config still require an EPP restart.
stance_target: operational constraint on any router customization strategy
quoted_support: The configuration is only read on startup. Any updates to the configuration require a restart of the EPP process to take effect.
